reviewType: Limited review of country-dependent Section 301 forced-labor Chapter 99 routing, not comprehensive classification or customs compliance certification.

officialSources.name: CBP CSMS #69326983 (July 23, 2026)
officialSources.finding: The 65 Chapter 99 origin headings 9903.05.20–9903.05.84 took effect July 24, 2026. 9903.05.30 is Chile, 9903.05.32 is Colombia (+12.5%), 9903.05.86 is a possible U.S. note 52(b) exception; 9903.05.85–9903.05.92 contain shared exclusions. Paired EU, JP, KR, CH and TW rates require Column 1 comparison.

officialSources.name: USITC 2026 HTS Revision 21
officialSources.finding: Revision 21 remains current. Screen rates from live USITC tariff rows where code-specific metadata is missing from bundled reverse index.

officialSources.name: Official Federal Register, 91 FR July 28, 2026
officialSources.finding: Heading 9903.05.32 is designated for Colombian goods with +12.5% subject to Note 52 exemptions.

implemented: Country-specific candidate dispatch across all 65 origin headings; unrelated country-specific codes are excluded from candidate list.
Use current USITC row to show the originating country heading even if the static reverse HTS index omitted it; if live row unavailable fail closed.
Column 1 positive surcharge is not zeroed by Column 2's 'No change'.
Origin-country baseline and Note 52 exemption candidates are not conflated; unresolved exception eligibility prevents a misleading confirmed total.
9903.01.30 donation provision no longer displays unrelated 2(a) Mexico note text; exact subdivision notes are cited.
Paired Chapter 99 treatments that depend on Column 1 rate are flagged for review instead of stacked.
regressionEvidence: Netlify preview #54 built successfully on Oct 28. GitHub Actions Chapter 99 origin regression tests passed against mocked USITC currentRevision and Chapter 99 rows, including 9903.05.32 Colombia vs 9903.05.30 Chile, Column 1 12.5%, and exclusion of Mexican Note 2(a) excerpt. Existing metal/vehicle Chapter 99 basis tests also passed.
exclusions: Only U.S. note 52 origin dispatch is reviewed; AD/CVD, quotas and ACE flags not reviewed.
All exemptions under U.S. note 52(b)-(k) require matching product/entry facts before a full total is declared.
Future dated tariff changes, including announced Oct 30 Canadian changes, still require additional legal data and tests.
No assertion that the calculator is suitable for actual filing or that every Chapter 99 interaction is resolved.
releaseDecision: Permit owner-requested correction for origin routing with unresolved measure review labeling preserved; no generic zero-duty assumption.
